      "text": "# Lecture Notes: Chemical Calculations \u0026 Neutralization Titration\n**Date:** November 26, 2025\n**Location:** Slovenia (Academic Context)\n**Subject:** [[General Chemistry]] / [[Stoichiometry]]\n\n---\n\n## 1. Colloquium Review: Problem Solving Analysis\n*Context: The lecture begins with a review of the recent colloquium (exam), addressing common mistakes and the correct methodology for solving the assigned problems.*\n\n### 1.1. Determination of Molecular Formula (Hydrocarbons)\n**Problem:** Calculate the true formula of a compound where carbon and hydrogen combine in a mass ratio of $1 : 0.0833$. The density of the vapor is $3.44\\, \\text{g/L}$ at $1.01\\, \\text{bar}$ and $90^\\circ\\text{C}$.\n\n**Derivation \u0026 Logic:**\n1.  **Empirical Formula:**\n    *   Ratio $m_C : m_H \u003d 1 : 0.0833$.\n    *   Divide by atomic masses ($A_r(C)\u003d12.01$, $A_r(H)\u003d1.008$) to get mole ratio:\n        $$ n_C : n_H \u003d \\frac{1}{12} : \\frac{0.0833}{1} \\approx 0.0833 : 0.0833 \u003d 1 : 1 $$\n    *   **Empirical Formula:** $CH$ (Molar mass unit $M_{emp} \u003d 13\\, \\text{g/mol}$).\n\n2.  **Molar Mass Calculation (Ideal Gas Law):**\n    *   The lecturer actively recalls the derivation from the [[Ideal Gas Law]]:\n        $$ PV \u003d nRT \\quad \\text{and} \\quad n \u003d \\frac{m}{M} $$\n        $$ PV \u003d \\frac{m}{M}RT \\implies P \u003d \\frac{m}{V} \\cdot \\frac{RT}{M} \\implies P \u003d \\rho \\frac{RT}{M} $$\n        $$ M \u003d \\frac{\\rho R T}{P} $$\n    *   **Input Data:**\n        *   $\\rho \u003d 3.44\\, \\text{g/L}$\n        *   $T \u003d 90^\\circ\\text{C} \u003d 363.15\\, \\text{K}$\n        *   $P \u003d 1.01\\, \\text{bar} \u003d 101\\, \\text{kPa}$\n        *   $R \u003d 8.314\\, \\text{J}/(\\text{mol K}) \u003d 8.314\\, (\\text{kPa L})/(\\text{mol K})$\n    *   **Calculation:**\n        $$ M \\approx \\frac{3.44 \\cdot 8.314 \\cdot 363}{101} \\approx 78\\, \\text{g/mol} $$\n\n3.  **Molecular Formula:**\n    *   Ratio $\\frac{M_{true}}{M_{emp}} \u003d \\frac{78}{13} \u003d 6$.\n    *   **Result:** $C_6H_6$ ([[Benzene]]).\n\n\u003e [!WARNING] Critical Analysis: Unit Consistency\n\u003e The most common error here is using the wrong Gas Constant ($R$) relative to the Pressure units.\n\u003e *   If $P$ is in **Pa**, $\\rho$ must be in **$\\text{kg/m}^3$**.\n\u003e *   If $P$ is in **kPa**, $\\rho$ can be in **$\\text{g/L}$**.\n\u003e *   Always convert Temperature to **Kelvin**.\n\n---\n\n### 1.2. Partial Pressures in Gas Mixtures\n**Problem:** Oxygen and Hydrogen mixture.\n**Formula:** [[Dalton\u0027s Law]] of Partial Pressures.\n$$ p_i \u003d x_i \\cdot P_{tot} $$\n*   $p_i$: Partial pressure of component $i$.\n*   $x_i$: Mole fraction ($\\frac{n_i}{n_{tot}}$).\n*   $P_{tot}$: Total pressure.\n\n**Key Concept:** The sum of mole fractions must always equal 1 ($x_{O_2} + x_{H_2} \u003d 1$).\n\n---\n\n### 1.3. Stoichiometry involving Gases (Mg + HCl)\n**Reaction:**\n$$ Mg_{(s)} + 2HCl_{(aq)} \\rightarrow MgCl_{2(aq)} + H_{2(g)} $$\n**Methodology:**\n1.  Calculate moles of the limiting reagent.\n2.  Use stoichiometry ratio ($1:1$ for $Mg:H_2$) to find moles of gas.\n3.  Use $V \u003d \\frac{nRT}{P}$ to find the volume of Hydrogen gas evolved.\n\n---\n\n### 1.4. Crystallization Water (Copper Sulfate)\n**Concept:** Calculating the mass of water lost when heating a hydrate ($CuSO_4 \\cdot 5H_2O \\to CuSO_4$).\n*   **Comparison:** Ratio of anhydrous salt mass to water mass vs. theoretical molar masses.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Neutralization Titration\n*Context: Introduction of the new laboratory topic. The lecturer transitions from static calculations to dynamic laboratory processes.*\n\n### 2.1. Theoretical Foundation\n**Definition:** A reaction where an acid and a base react to form a salt and water.\n$$ \\text{Acid} + \\text{Base} \\rightarrow \\text{Salt} + \\text{Water} $$\n\n**The Net Ionic Equation:**\n$$ H^+_{(aq)} + OH^-_{(aq)} \\rightarrow H_2O_{(l)} $$\n\n**Equivalence Point:** The point where the amount of added titrant is stoichiometrically equivalent to the analyte.\n*   **Indicators:** Used to visualize the endpoint (e.g., Methyl Orange, Phenolphthalein).\n\n### 2.2. Titration of Carbonates (Gas Evolution)\nWhen titrating carbonates with strong acids, carbonic acid is formed, which is unstable and decomposes:\n$$ Na_2CO_3 + H_2SO_4 \\rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + H_2CO_3 $$\n$$ H_2CO_3 \\rightleftharpoons H_2O + CO_2 \\uparrow $$\n\n\u003e [!NOTE] Tutor\u0027s Insight: Why gas matters?\n\u003e The evolution of gas ($CO_2$ or $H_2S$ in sulfide titrations) drives the reaction to completion according to [[Le Chatelier\u0027s Principle]] by removing a product from the system.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Detailed Solving of Titration Problems\n*Reverse engineering the handwritten notes provided in the source material.*\n\n### 3.1. Standardization of Sulfuric Acid\n**Task:** Determine the concentration of a sulfuric acid solution using a standard sodium carbonate solution.\n\n**Data Provided:**\n*   **Analyte:** $Na_2CO_3$\n    *   Volume ($V_{base}$) \u003d $25\\, \\text{mL}$\n    *   Mass Concentration ($\\gamma$) \u003d $5\\, \\text{g/L}$\n*   **Titrant:** $H_2SO_4$\n    *   Volume ($V_{acid}$) consumed \u003d $22.3\\, \\text{mL}$\n\n**Step-by-Step Calculation:**\n\n1.  **Determine Molar Concentration of $Na_2CO_3$:**\n    $$ c \u003d \\frac{\\gamma}{M} $$\n    *   $M(Na_2CO_3) \u003d 2\\cdot23 + 12 + 3\\cdot16 \\approx 106\\, \\text{g/mol}$\n    *   $c(Na_2CO_3) \u003d \\frac{5\\, \\text{g/L}}{106\\, \\text{g/mol}} \u003d 0.04717\\, \\text{mol/L}$\n\n2.  **Stoichiometry:**\n    $$ Na_2CO_3 + H_2SO_4 \\rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + CO_2 + H_2O $$\n    *   Ratio $n(Na_2CO_3) : n(H_2SO_4) \u003d 1 : 1$.\n    *   Therefore: $c_{base} \\cdot V_{base} \u003d c_{acid} \\cdot V_{acid}$.\n\n3.  **Calculate Acid Concentration ($c_{acid}$):**\n    $$ c_{acid} \u003d \\frac{c_{base} \\cdot V_{base}}{V_{acid}} $$\n    $$ c(H_2SO_4) \u003d \\frac{0.04717\\, \\text{M} \\cdot 25\\, \\text{mL}}{22.3\\, \\text{mL}} $$\n    $$ c(H_2SO_4) \\approx 0.0529\\, \\text{mol/L} $$\n\n---\n\n### 3.2. The \"Aliquot\" Problem (Barium Chloride)\n**Task:** Precipitation titration involving dilution.\n\n**Scenario:**\n1.  Weigh $15\\, \\text{g}$ of $BaCl_2 \\cdot 2H_2O$.\n2.  Dissolve in water and dilute to a total volume of **$250\\, \\text{mL}$** (Volumetric Flask).\n3.  Take a **$15\\, \\text{mL}$** sample (aliquot) for titration.\n4.  Titrate with $AgNO_3$ ($c\u003d0.1\\, \\text{M}$).\n\n**Calculation Logic:**\n1.  **Calculate Molar Mass:**\n    *   $M(BaCl_2 \\cdot 2H_2O) \u003d 137.3 + 2\\cdot35.5 + 2\\cdot18 \\approx 244.3\\, \\text{g/mol}$.\n2.  **Calculate Moles in Initial Flask ($250\\, \\text{mL}$):**\n    $$ n_{total} \u003d \\frac{m}{M} \u003d \\frac{15}{244.3} \\approx 0.0614\\, \\text{mol} $$\n3.  **Calculate Concentration of Barium Chloride:**\n    $$ c(BaCl_2) \u003d \\frac{n_{total}}{V_{flask}} \u003d \\frac{0.0614}{0.25\\, \\text{L}} \u003d 0.2456\\, \\text{mol/L} $$\n4.  **Titration of Aliquot ($15\\, \\text{mL}$):**\n    *   Reaction: $BaCl_2 + 2AgNO_3 \\to 2AgCl + Ba(NO_3)_2$.\n    *   Stoichiometry: $n(AgNO_3) \u003d 2 \\cdot n(BaCl_2)$.\n    *   $c_{Ag} V_{Ag} \u003d 2 \\cdot (c_{Ba} V_{Ba\\_aliquot})$.\n    *   Solve for $V(AgNO_3)$.\n\n\u003e [!WARNING] Aliquot Trap\n\u003e Students often calculate the moles for the *entire* 250 mL flask and use that in the titration formula. You must calculate the **concentration** first (which is constant) or calculate the specific moles in the **15 mL aliquot**.\n\n---\n\n### 3.3. Dilution Calculation\n**Problem:** How much water must be added to dilute a solution to a target concentration?\n**Formula:**\n$$ c_1 V_1 \u003d c_2 V_2 $$\n*   $c_1, V_1$: Initial state.\n*   $c_2, V_2$: Final state.\n*   **Added Solvent:** $V_{added} \u003d V_2 - V_1$.\n\n**Specific Example from Notes:**\n*   Target: Prepare $1\\, \\text{L}$ of solution with $c \u003d 0.05\\, \\text{M}$.\n*   Stock: You have the $H_2SO_4$ calculated previously ($0.0529\\, \\text{M}$).\n*   *Correction:* The lecture implies solving for how much of the *original* is needed or how much to dilute.\n    $$ V_{required} \u003d \\frac{c_{target} \\cdot V_{target}}{c_{stock}} $$\n\n---\n\n## 4. General Formulas \u0026 Identities\n\n### Stoichiometry\n*   **Mole:** $n \u003d \\frac{m}{M}$\n*   **Molar Concentration:** $c \u003d \\frac{n}{V}$\n*   **Mass Concentration:** $\\gamma \u003d \\frac{m_{solute}}{V_{solution}} \u003d c \\cdot M$\n*   **Dilution:** $c_1 V_1 \u003d c_2 V_2$\n\n### Gas Laws\n*   **Ideal Gas Law:** $PV \u003d nRT$\n*   **Density of Gas:** $\\rho \u003d \\frac{PM}{RT}$\n*   **Standard Conditions (STP):** Usually $T\u003d273.15\\, \\text{K}$, $P\u003d100\\, \\text{kPa}$ (or $101.325\\, \\text{kPa}$ depending on convention used in class).\n\n### Titration (General)\nFor reaction $aA + bB \\to \\dots$\n$$ \\frac{c_A V_A}{a} \u003d \\frac{c_B V_B}{b} $$\n\n---\n*Tags: #chemistry #titration #stoichiometry #obsidian-notes #university*",

        "text": "}$).\n\n2.  **Molar Mass Calculation (Ideal Gas Law):**\n    *   The lecturer actively recalls the derivation from"
      }, {
        "text": " the [[Ideal Gas Law]]:\n        $$ PV \u003d nRT \\quad \\text{and} \\quad n \u003d \\"
      }, {
        "text": "frac{m}{M} $$\n        $$ PV \u003d \\frac{m}{M}RT \\implies P \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " \\frac{m}{V} \\cdot \\frac{RT}{M} \\implies P \u003d \\rho \\frac"
      }, {
        "text": "{RT}{M} $$\n        $$ M \u003d \\frac{\\rho R T}{P} $$\n    *"
      }, {
        "text": "   **Input Data:**\n        *   $\\rho \u003d 3.44\\, \\text{g/L"
      }, {
        "text": "}$\n        *   $T \u003d 90^\\circ\\text{C} \u003d 363.15\\, \\text"
      }, {
        "text": "{K}$\n        *   $P \u003d 1.01\\, \\text{bar} \u003d 10"
      }, {
        "text": "1\\, \\text{kPa}$\n        *   $R \u003d 8.314\\, \\text{"
      }, {
        "text": "J}/(\\text{mol K}) \u003d 8.314\\, (\\text{kPa L})/(\\text{mol K})$\n    "
      }, {
        "text": "*   **Calculation:**\n        $$ M \\approx \\frac{3.44 \\cdot 8.3"
      }, {
        "text": "14 \\cdot 363}{101} \\approx 78\\, \\text{g/mol"
      }, {
        "text": "} $$\n\n3.  **Molecular Formula:**\n    *   Ratio $\\frac{M_{true}}{M_{emp}} \u003d \\frac{"
      }, {
        "text": "78}{13} \u003d 6$.\n    *   **Result:** $C_6H_6"
      }, {
        "text": "$ ([[Benzene]]).\n\n\u003e [!WARNING] Critical Analysis: Unit Consistency\n\u003e The most common error here is using"
      }, {
        "text": " the wrong Gas Constant ($R$) relative to the Pressure units.\n\u003e *   If $P$ is in **Pa"
      }, {
        "text": "**, $\\rho$ must be in **$\\text{kg/m}^3$**.\n\u003e *   If $P$ is in **kPa**,"
      }, {
        "text": " $\\rho$ can be in **$\\text{g/L}$**.\n\u003e *   Always convert Temperature to **Kelvin**.\n\n---"
      }, {
        "text": "\n\n### 1.2. Partial Pressures in Gas Mixtures\n**Problem:** Oxygen and Hydrogen mixture.\n**Formula"
      }, {
        "text": ":** [[Dalton\u0027s Law]] of Partial Pressures.\n$$ p_i \u003d x_i \\cdot P"
      }, {
        "text": "_{tot} $$\n*   $p_i$: Partial pressure of component $i$.\n*   $x_"
      }, {
        "text": "i$: Mole fraction ($\\frac{n_i}{n_{tot}}$).\n*   $P_{tot}$: Total pressure."
      }, {
        "text": "\n\n**Key Concept:** The sum of mole fractions must always equal 1 ($x_{O_2} + x_{"
      }, {
        "text": "H_2} \u003d 1$).\n\n---\n\n### 1.3. Stoichiometry involving Gases (Mg + HCl)\n**Reaction"
      }, {
        "text": ":**\n$$ Mg_{(s)} + 2HCl_{(aq)} \\rightarrow MgCl_{2(aq)} + H_{"
      }, {
        "text": "2(g)} $$\n**Methodology:**\n1.  Calculate moles of the limiting reagent.\n2.  Use stoichiometry"
      }, {
        "text": " ratio ($1:1$ for $Mg:H_2$) to find moles of gas.\n3.  Use $"
      }, {
        "text": "V \u003d \\frac{nRT}{P}$ to find the volume of Hydrogen gas evolved.\n\n---\n\n### 1."
      }, {
        "text": "4. Crystallization Water (Copper Sulfate)\n**Concept:** Calculating the mass of water lost when heating a hydrate ($"
      }, {
        "text": "CuSO_4 \\cdot 5H_2O \\to CuSO_4$).\n*   **Comparison:** Ratio"
      }, {
        "text": " of anhydrous salt mass to water mass vs. theoretical molar masses.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Neutralization Titration\n"
      }, {
        "text": "*Context: Introduction of the new laboratory topic. The lecturer transitions from static calculations to dynamic laboratory processes.*\n\n### 2.1"
      }, {
        "text": ". Theoretical Foundation\n**Definition:** A reaction where an acid and a base react to form a salt and water.\n$$ \\text{"
      }, {
        "text": "Acid} + \\text{Base} \\rightarrow \\text{Salt} + \\text{Water} $$\n\n**The"
      }, {
        "text": " Net Ionic Equation:**\n$$ H^+_{(aq)} + OH^-_{(aq)} \\rightarrow H_2O_{(l)} $$\n\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "Equivalence Point:** The point where the amount of added titrant is stoichiometrically equivalent to the analyte.\n*   **Indicators:** Used to"
      }, {
        "text": " visualize the endpoint (e.g., Methyl Orange, Phenolphthalein).\n\n### 2.2. Tit"
      }, {
        "text": "ration of Carbonates (Gas Evolution)\nWhen titrating carbonates with strong acids, carbonic acid is formed, which is unstable and decomposes:"
      }, {
        "text": "\n$$ Na_2CO_3 + H_2SO_4 \\rightarrow Na_2SO_4 +"
      }, {
        "text": " H_2CO_3 $$\n$$ H_2CO_3 \\rightleftharpoons H_2O + CO_2 \\uparrow $$\n\n\u003e"
      }, {
        "text": " [!NOTE] Tutor\u0027s Insight: Why gas matters?\n\u003e The evolution of gas ($CO_2$ or $H_2"
      }, {
        "text": "S$ in sulfide titrations) drives the reaction to completion according to [[Le Chatelier\u0027s Principle]] by removing a"
      }, {
        "text": " product from the system.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Detailed Solving of Titration Problems\n*Reverse engineering the handwritten notes provided"
      }, {
        "text": " in the source material.*\n\n### 3.1. Standardization of Sulfuric Acid\n**Task:** Determine the concentration of a"
      }, {
        "text": " sulfuric acid solution using a standard sodium carbonate solution.\n\n**Data Provided:**\n*   **Analyte:** $Na_2CO"
      }, {
        "text": "_3$\n    *   Volume ($V_{base}$) \u003d $25\\, \\text{mL}$\n    *   Mass"
      }, {
        "text": " Concentration ($\\gamma$) \u003d $5\\, \\text{g/L}$\n*   **Titrant:** $H_2SO_"
      }, {
        "text": "4$\n    *   Volume ($V_{acid}$) consumed \u003d $22.3\\, \\text{mL}$\n\n**Step-"
      }, {
        "text": "by-Step Calculation:**\n\n1.  **Determine Molar Concentration of $Na_2CO_3$:**\n    $$ c \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " \\frac{\\gamma}{M} $$\n    *   $M(Na_2CO_3) \u003d "
      }, {
        "text": "2\\cdot23 + 12 + 3\\cdot16 \\approx 106\\, \\text{g/"
      }, {
        "text": "mol}$\n    *   $c(Na_2CO_3) \u003d \\frac{5\\, \\text"
      }, {
        "text": "{g/L}}{106\\, \\text{g/mol}} \u003d 0.0471"
      }, {
        "text": "7\\, \\text{mol/L}$\n\n2.  **Stoichiometry:**\n    $$ Na_2CO_3 + H"
      }, {
        "text": "_2SO_4 \\rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + CO_2 + H_2O $$\n    *   Ratio"
      }, {
        "text": " $n(Na_2CO_3) : n(H_2SO_4) \u003d 1 :"
      }, {
        "text": " 1$.\n    *   Therefore: $c_{base} \\cdot V_{base} \u003d c_{acid} \\"
      }, {
        "text": "cdot V_{acid}$.\n\n3.  **Calculate Acid Concentration ($c_{acid}$):**\n    $$ c"
      }, {
        "text": "_{acid} \u003d \\frac{c_{base} \\cdot V_{base}}{V_{acid}} $$\n    "
      }, {
        "text": "$$ c(H_2SO_4) \u003d \\frac{0.04717\\, \\text{M"
      }, {
        "text": "} \\cdot 25\\, \\text{mL}}{22.3\\, \\text{mL}} $$\n    $$ c(H"
      }, {
        "text": "_2SO_4) \\approx 0.0529\\, \\text{mol/L} $$\n\n---"
      }, {
        "text": "\n\n### 3.2. The \"Aliquot\" Problem (Barium Chloride)\n**Task:** Precipitation titration involving dilution"
      }, {
        "text": ".\n\n**Scenario:**\n1.  Weigh $15\\, \\text{g}$ of $BaCl_2 \\cdot"
      }, {
        "text": " 2H_2O$.\n2.  Dissolve in water and dilute to a total volume of **$250\\, \\text{"
      }, {
        "text": "mL}$** (Volumetric Flask).\n3.  Take a **$15\\, \\text{mL}$** sample (al"
      }, {
        "text": "iquot) for titration.\n4.  Titrate with $AgNO_3$ ($c\u003d0."
      }, {
        "text": "1\\, \\text{M}$).\n\n**Calculation Logic:**\n1.  **Calculate Molar Mass:**\n    *"
      }, {
        "text": "   $M(BaCl_2 \\cdot 2H_2O) \u003d 137.3 + 2"
      }, {
        "text": "\\cdot35.5 + 2\\cdot18 \\approx 244.3\\, \\text{g/mol"
      }, {
        "text": "}$.\n2.  **Calculate Moles in Initial Flask ($250\\, \\text{mL}$):**\n    $$ n_{"
      }, {
        "text": "total} \u003d \\frac{m}{M} \u003d \\frac{15}{244.3} \\approx"
      }, {
        "text": " 0.0614\\, \\text{mol} $$\n3.  **Calculate Concentration of Barium Chloride"
      }, {
        "text": ":**\n    $$ c(BaCl_2) \u003d \\frac{n_{total}}{V_{flask}} \u003d \\frac{0.0"
      }, {
        "text": "614}{0.25\\, \\text{L}} \u003d 0.2456\\, \\text{mol/L}"
      }, {
        "text": " $$\n4.  **Titration of Aliquot ($15\\, \\text{mL}$):**\n    *"
      }, {
        "text": "   Reaction: $BaCl_2 + 2AgNO_3 \\to 2AgCl + Ba("
      }, {
        "text": "NO_3)_2$.\n    *   Stoichiometry: $n(AgNO_3) \u003d 2 \\"
      }, {
        "text": "cdot n(BaCl_2)$.\n    *   $c_{Ag} V_{Ag} \u003d 2 \\cdot"
      }, {
        "text": " (c_{Ba} V_{Ba\\_aliquot})$.\n    *   Solve for $V(AgNO_3)$.\n\n\u003e ["
      }, {
        "text": "!WARNING] Aliquot Trap\n\u003e Students often calculate the moles for the *entire* 250 mL"
      }, {
        "text": " flask and use that in the titration formula. You must calculate the **concentration** first (which is constant) or calculate the"
      }, {
        "text": " specific moles in the **15 mL aliquot**.\n\n---\n\n### 3.3. Dilution Calculation\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "Problem:** How much water must be added to dilute a solution to a target concentration?\n**Formula:**\n$$ c_1 V_1 \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " c_2 V_2 $$\n*   $c_1, V_1$: Initial state.\n*   $c_2"
      }, {
        "text": ", V_2$: Final state.\n*   **Added Solvent:** $V_{added} \u003d V_2 - V_1"
      }, {
        "text": "$.\n\n**Specific Example from Notes:**\n*   Target: Prepare $1\\, \\text{L}$ of solution with $c \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " 0.05\\, \\text{M}$.\n*   Stock: You have the $H_2SO_4$ calculated"
      }, {
        "text": " previously ($0.0529\\, \\text{M}$).\n*   *Correction:* The lecture implies solving for how"
      }, {
        "text": " much of the *original* is needed or how much to dilute.\n    $$ V_{required} \u003d \\frac{c_{"
      }, {
        "text": "target} \\cdot V_{target}}{c_{stock}} $$\n\n---\n\n## 4. General Formulas \u0026 Identities\n\n### Sto"
      }, {
        "text": "ichiometry\n*   **Mole:** $n \u003d \\frac{m}{M}$\n*   **Molar Concentration:** $c \u003d \\frac"
      }, {
        "text": "{n}{V}$\n*   **Mass Concentration:** $\\gamma \u003d \\frac{m_{solute}}{V_{solution}} \u003d"
      }, {
        "text": " c \\cdot M$\n*   **Dilution:** $c_1 V_1 \u003d c_2 V"
      }, {
        "text": "_2$\n\n### Gas Laws\n*   **Ideal Gas Law:** $PV \u003d nRT$\n*   **Density"
      }, {
        "text": " of Gas:** $\\rho \u003d \\frac{PM}{RT}$\n*   **Standard Conditions (STP):** Usually"
      }, {
        "text": " $T\u003d273.15\\, \\text{K}$, $P\u003d100\\, \\text"
      }, {
        "text": "{kPa}$ (or $101.325\\, \\text{kPa}$ depending on convention used in"
      }, {
        "text": " class).\n\n### Titration (General)\nFor reaction $aA + bB \\to \\dots$\n$$ \\frac{c"
      }, {
        "text": "_A V_A}{a} \u003d \\frac{c_B V_B}{b} $$\n\n---\n*"
      }, {
